source.title: The Role of Variability in Motor Learning.

confidence_rationale: Authoritative review (Annu Rev Neurosci) consolidating human + animal evidence that motor variability is a regulated FEATURE -- purposeful exploration of behavior space that, coupled with reinforcement, drives learning -- not unwanted noise. Maps with high fidelity onto the MECH-442 premise that behavioral diversity must be actively maintained (not a side-effect) to be useful. Caps below 0.8 because it grounds the necessity-and-regulation of diversity, not the specific archive-survives-the-commit-gate mechanism.
failure_signatures: Variability is framed as exploration of motor space coupled to reinforcement, which is a noise-then-select picture (generate-and-reinforce), NOT a per-niche-elite archive that survives selection -- so it supports diversity-must-be-maintained without endorsing the specific MAP-Elites structure.
The review notes variability is regulated structurally (task-dependent, dimension-specific), which warns that a single uniform behavioral-descriptor may be the wrong granularity.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Trial-to-trial motor variability is not merely a consequence of a noisy nervous system; sensorimotor systems treat variability as purposeful, actively-regulated exploration of motor space that, coupled with reinforcement, drives motor learning, with dedicated neural circuits generating and regulating it.
mapping.ree_translation: REE's requirement that behavioral diversity be a maintained, structured property (behavioral_diversity_isolation:GAP-B) -- rather than a side-effect of selection -- is biologically grounded: the nervous system maintains and regulates behavioral variability as a feature, which is the necessity MECH-442's archive (and the ARC-065 generation pathway it preserves) instantiates.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The review grounds the diversity-is-a-regulated-feature necessity and an explore-then-reinforce loop, NOT the specific claim that diversity survives the commit step via a per-niche-elite archive; it is consistent with (but does not uniquely support) the MAP-Elites structure over a simple variability-injection-plus-selection account.
mapping.source_context: Review across human psychophysics and animal (songbird, rodent) motor-learning models; reinforcement-learning framing of motor variability.

confidence_components.notes: High-tier review; mapping_fidelity good for the necessity-and-regulation premise; transfer_risk lower because the claim is about the general principle (variability as regulated feature) which transfers cleanly to REE's diversity-must-reach-behavior requirement.
